entries.title: Asking every day
entries.literal_meaning: For the person who asks every day, there is no giver.
entries.explanation: The daily asking meets an absolute “no giver” in the answering half. The dictionary defines the daily asker; it does not explain why help is needed or absent. Our reading considers the impatience that repetition can provoke, while questioning whether repeated need makes someone undeserving. Deliberate refusal is a possible interpretation, not an action established by the wording.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରତିଦିନ ମାଗିବାର ଉତ୍ତରରେ କଥାଟି ଦେବାଲୋକର ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଭାବ ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ନିତି ମାଗିବାକୁ ଆସୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନ ମିଳିବାର କାରଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବାରମ୍ବାର ଅନୁରୋଧରୁ ଜନ୍ମିପାରୁଥିବା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ। ପୁଣି ମାଗିଲେ ବୋଲି କେହି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ କି? ଜାଣିଶୁଣି ମନା କରିବା ଏକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପଢ଼ା, ଶବ୍ଦରୁ ସ୍ଥିର ହୋଇଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Daily asking meets no giver; our reading considers impatience without assuming its cause.
entries.odia_summary: ନିତି ମାଗିଲେ ଦେବାଲୋକ ନାହିଁ; ତାହାର କାରଣ ନ ଧରି ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A neighbour repeatedly borrows a chair for evening lessons. Someone quotes the saying in irritation. Another asks whether they could agree on a regular arrangement instead. The invented reply questions the refusal; it does not establish a traditional answer.
entries.cultural_context: The source names no class or community. Its categorical wording is not evidence that people in continuing need are unworthy or that assistance is always refused.

entries.odia: କାହାର କି ଚିନ୍ତା, ବାଇଣ୍ଟି ପୋଇଲିର ଘଇତା ଚିନ୍ତା
entries.title: Everyone has a concern
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever others worry about, the girl addressed with this taunt worries about a husband.
entries.explanation: The opening leaves everyone else’s concerns unspecified, then singles out a girl’s interest in a husband for teasing. The dictionary calls the address mild abuse used by mothers towards young girls. Our critical reading notices the unequal permission to have a concern: her interest becomes the joke. It does not turn the insult into an affectionate nickname or establish what any girl actually wants.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆରମ୍ଭରେ ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ; ଶେଷରେ ଝିଅର ସ୍ୱାମୀଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଟାହି କରାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ସମ୍ବୋଧନକୁ ମାଆମାନେ ଟୋକୀ ଝିଅଙ୍କୁ ଦେଉଥିବା ଗାଳି ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ—ନିଜ ଚିନ୍ତା ରଖିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ସମାନ ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାର ଆଗ୍ରହ ହସର କଥା ହୁଏ। ଗାଳିକୁ ସ୍ନେହନାମ କରାଯାଉନାହିଁ, କୌଣସି ଝିଅର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଇଚ୍ଛା ମଧ୍ୟ ଧରାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The taunt singles out a girl’s concern; our critical reading questions that scrutiny.
entries.odia_summary: ଝିଅର ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଟାହି କରିବାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A reading group compares how different people’s interests become jokes. One reader quotes the line; another asks why the girl’s interest is singled out while everyone else’s remains unnamed. This is a present-day invented discussion, not a collected family conversation.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary marks Ganjam usage, not an exclusive origin or a practice of every family. The abusive expression remains in the exact witness; no community or gender trait is inferred.

entries.title: The world in two colours
entries.explanation: This brief expression offers a contrast without naming its two sides. The dictionary explains the headword through opposite colours or different pictures. Our reading treats the world’s changing appearance as an invitation to compare experiences, not proof that everyone is deceitful. A cheerful public occasion and difficult work behind it are one editorial application, not the source’s prescribed pair.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ କଥାଟି ଦୁଇ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ନାମ ନ ଦେଇ ବିରୋଧର ଚିତ୍ର ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ବିପରୀତ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣ ବା ଭିନ୍ନ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଶବ୍ଦଟିକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଦୁନିଆର ଭିନ୍ନ ଦେଖା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ମେଳାଇ ଦେଖିବାକୁ କୁହେ; ସବୁ ଲୋକ ଛଳନାକାରୀ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆନନ୍ଦମୟ ଅନୁଷ୍ଠାନ ଓ ପଛର କଠିନ କାମ ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ, ଉତ୍ସ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ କରିଥିବା ଯୋଡ଼ି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A short image of contrast leaves its two sides open; our example supplies one pair.
entries.odia_summary: ବିରୋଧର ଛୋଟ ଚିତ୍ର; ଦୁଇ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱକୁ ଆମ ଉଦାହରଣ ପୂରଣ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a neighbourhood celebration, two volunteers see the bright photographs and the pile of chairs still to be stacked. One recalls the two-coloured-world expression. They mean the contrast between the public occasion and its remaining work, not dishonesty by the guests.
entries.cultural_context: A short dictionary-labelled aphoristic expression, not a recovered longer proverb. No fixed moral, traditional performance setting or universal human trait is supplied.
